decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed officially raised interest rates following solid job gains and continued economic growth.

changes.quote: Averaging through hurricane-related fluctuations, job gains have been solid, and the unemployment rate declined further.
changes.explanation: Temporary storm disruptions have passed, revealing a strong underlying job market.

changes.quote: Voting against the action were Charles L. Evans and Neel Kashkari, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate.
changes.explanation: Two officials disagreed with the rate hike and voted to keep rates steady.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in November indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate.
On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have declined this year and are running below 2 percent.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.08% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.36% and moved -4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.9% would fall by about $6.87 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.2%, and employers added an average of 151k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.2% over the past year (November 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -4 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.05%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.22% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed plans to continue making gradual increases in the federal funds rate as economic conditions evolve. Educational forecast models suggest a 66% chance of a hold and a 33% chance of a hike at the next meeting.
